title: daily-scratchpad-gpu-ops-21
content:
Quick notes + running TODOs for GPU ops context (personal scratchpad)

Context:
- Weekly capacity sync + node replacement window coming up next Tue. Need to finalize N+1 plan for p4d and a100 pools.
- Observed intermittent OOMs on long-run batch jobs (embedding refresh). Suspect kv-cache leak or batch-size drift after runtime update.

Top priorities (this sprint)
- [ ] Finalize capacity numbers for Q2 reserved pool (target: +25% throughput for burst workloads). draft calc below.
- [ ] Validate kernel + driver matrix on staging nodes (a100 v6/GPU driver 535.xx). Rollback plan if regressions.
- [ ] Fix INFRA-512 network egress rule that blocks health checks between us-west-1 subnets. Short-term firewall patch, long-term policy.
- [ ] Re-run embedding refresh with smaller batch sizes + KV cache flush to repro OOMs. Log pid, timeline, memory RSS.
- [ ] Check cold-start latency after enabling prefix cache TTL=30s on dedicated runtime.

Notes / scratch debugging items:
- Capacity calc (rough): current sustained tokens/sec = 120k, peak = 210k. Q2 target sustained = 150k, peak = 260k. Need ~18 additional a100 nodes or 6 p4d equivalence (w/ batching tweaks). Confirm pricing for dedicated contracts.
- Suspect cause for OOM: new runtime change (commit 7f3a2c) changed continuous batching behavior — batches not being compacted correctly for long context. Add logging around batch sizes at enqueue + dequeue.
- Driver matrix tested on staging (2026-03-02):
  * a100 nodes: driver 535.54 + cudnn 9.1 -> passes single-token smoke + 1k token run
  * p4d nodes: driver 525.85 + cudnn 8.4 -> flaky on 2k token runs (GPU mem fragmentation)
  Action: schedule deeper stress test 4h window 03/04 22:00 UTC.

Networking reminders:
- Health-checks: ALB -> target group -> node port 8081. Need to add healthcheck timeout 6s for longer cold-starts.
- Egress rule (INFRA-512): missing cross-subnet allow for 10.12.0.0/16 -> 10.13.0.0/16. Patch id: fw-246. Coordinate with SRE (Ethan).

Oncall log snippets:
- 03/02 03:14 UTC: alert runout-high-memory on embedding-refresh job. Restarted job + flushed prefix cache. Temporary relief.
- 03/02 03:55 UTC: spike in GPU utilization coincident with model rollout v2.1. Reverted rollout -> utilization normalized.

Action plan for today (03/04):
- Morning: triage INFRA-512 + deploy temporary firewall patch (coord w/ SRE)
- Midday: run stress test on staging (22:00 UTC prep) -> collect perf + mem traces
- Afternoon: update capacity spreadsheet + send draft numbers to product for Q2 commit
- Evening: re-run embedding refresh smaller batches, capture logs to s3 (s3://redwood-ops/gpu-ops/debug/2026-03-04)

Misc notes / things to remember:
- Bring up question for capacity sync: reserve buffer for cache-heavy workloads (recommend 15% over token-based calc)
- Check quota limits with cloud provider before expanding p4d pool (region us-west-1 quota is 40 GPUs currently)
- Follow up with Lina on dedicated contract pricing negotiation (she has vendor contact)

Quick commands to run (for me later):
- ssh jump -> sudo journalctl -u inference-runtime -f --since "10 minutes ago"
- python infra/tools/trace_mem.py --job-id abc123 --out s3://redwood-ops/gpu-ops/debug/
- kubectl exec -n infra svc/runtime-staging -- env | grep GPU

Random thoughts (brain dump):
- Maybe useful to add a lightweight memory dump hook for long-running batches (post-mortem)
- Could limit batch growth by soft cap + fallback to smaller batch path when growth > X tokens/sec

End of scratchpad. Update after staging stress test and firewall patch.
